items.followUp: Why do noble gases have very low chemical reactivity?

rubric.why: The answer identifies the stable, complete outer electron shell of noble gases.
rubric.how: Award for stating that noble gases have a complete outermost shell or stable electronic configuration.

rubric.why: The answer explains that the stable shell means noble gases have little tendency to form bonds.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that noble gases do not readily gain, lose, or share electrons.

modelAnswer: Noble gases have a complete outermost electron shell, so they have a stable electronic configuration.
They have little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons; therefore, they are not reactive.

items.followUp: How does shielding affect the ionisation energy of an atom?

rubric.why: The answer identifies the shielding of the nucleus by inner-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award for stating that inner-shell electrons shield valence electrons from the nuclear attraction.

rubric.why: The answer links shielding to easier removal of a valence electron and cation formation.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that reduced attraction lowers ionisation energy, making cation formation easier.

modelAnswer: Inner-shell electrons shield the outermost electrons from the full attraction of the nucleus.
The outermost electrons are held less strongly and are removed more easily, so cations form more readily.

items.followUp: How are elements arranged in groups and periods in the Periodic Table?

rubric.why: This gives the orientation of groups in the Periodic Table.
rubric.how: Award for defining groups as vertical columns.

rubric.why: This gives the orientation of periods in the Periodic Table.
rubric.how: Award for defining periods as horizontal rows.

modelAnswer: Groups are the vertical columns of the Periodic Table.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the Periodic Table.

items.followUp: Write any two properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: This is one characteristic of many covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that covalent compounds generally have low melting points or low boiling points.

rubric.why: This is another accepted characteristic of covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award for any one other correct property, such as poor electrical conductivity, insolubility in water, solubility in organic solvents, or being gases, liquids, or soft solids.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They are usually poor conductors of electricity.

items.followUp: What is a double covalent bond? Give one example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Meaning of a triple covalent bond
rubric.how: Award for stating that three pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.

rubric.why: Nitrogen is a correct example of a molecule with a triple covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award for giving nitrogen, N₂, or N≡N as an example.

modelAnswer: A triple covalent bond is formed when two atoms share three pairs of electrons.

items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds generally have high melting points?

rubric.why: The answer identifies the oppositely charged ions that make up an ionic solid.
rubric.how: Award for stating that an ionic compound consists of positive and negative ions arranged in a lattice.

rubric.why: Strong attraction between ions holds the solid together and accounts for its solid state.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that strong electrostatic attraction between the ions holds them firmly together.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds consist of positive and negative ions arranged in a crystal lattice.
Strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions hold them firmly in fixed positions, so ionic compounds are solids.

items.followUp: What is meant by diffusion of gases?

accept: ability of gas molecules to move
move from one place to another
rubric.why: The answer describes the movement or freedom of movement of gas molecules.
rubric.how: Award for defining mobility as the ability of gas molecules to move freely or from place to place.

rubric.why: The answer adds that gas molecules move freely and randomly in all directions.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning that gas molecules move randomly or in all directions.

modelAnswer: Mobility of gases is the ability of gas molecules to move freely from one place to another.
Gas molecules move randomly in all directions.

items.followUp: A solution contains 12 g of solute in 80 g of solution. Calculate its mass/mass percentage.

accept: mass of solute divided by mass of solution
rubric.why: The answer identifies the ratio used to calculate mass/mass percentage.
rubric.how: Award for stating that mass/mass percentage is based on the mass of solute divided by the mass of solution.

accept: mass of solute divided by mass of solution multiplied by 100
rubric.why: Multiplying the ratio by 100 expresses the concentration as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award for including multiplication by 100 or stating that it is the mass of solute in 100 g of solution.

modelAnswer: Mass/mass % = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100.
It is the mass of solute present in 100 g of solution.
